question: Select the most appropriate hydrogen atom radius from the given options.
solution:
The correct answer is __**10⁻¹⁰ m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The radius of a hydrogen atom is approximately **0.53 Ångström (Å)**, which is equivalent to 0.53 x 10⁻¹⁰ meters.
 
• This value is based on the **Bohr radius**, which is a fundamental physical constant.
 
• The Bohr radius is derived from the basic principles of quantum mechanics and is crucial for understanding atomic structure.
 
• Hydrogen, being the simplest atom with one proton and one electron, has its electron orbit at this average distance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bohr Radius:**

 
 
• The Bohr radius is a physical constant approximately equal to 0.529 x 10⁻¹⁰ meters.
 
• It represents the most probable distance between the nucleus and the electron in a hydrogen atom in its ground state.
 
 
 
• **Ångström (Å):**
 
 
• An Ångström is a unit of length equal to 10⁻¹⁰ meters or 0.1 nanometers.
 
• It is commonly used to express atomic and molecular dimensions.
 
 
 
• **Quantum Mechanics:**
 
 
• Quantum mechanics is the fundamental theory in physics describing the behavior of matter and energy on atomic and subatomic scales.
 
• It underpins the calculation of atomic structures, including the hydrogen atom.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Atom:**
 
 
• The hydrogen atom is the simplest atom, consisting of one proton and one electron.
 
• Its simplicity makes it a fundamental model for studying atomic physics and quantum mechanics.
